method: Static reconstruction only: atomscan slow/no-update, cleave facts, AES/XOR reconstruction, dnfile/dncil CIL tracing, rizin x86 tracing. No sample execution or C2 retrieval.

samples.identification: Obfuscated Visual Basic XWorm V3.0 client
samples.marker_line: XWorm V3: RAT tasking and DDoS; add screen, cleanup and shutdown
evidence: Entrypoint MethodDef 0x26 at RVA 0x2678 sleeps, decrypts settings, writes an HKCU Run value pointing to an AppData self-copy, and starts the connect/receive workers. The settings decoder at RVA 0x4524 derives a 32-byte key from MD5(seed) copied at offsets 0 and 15, then uses Rijndael ECB; static reconstruction yields sh67h.fun:2083, packet separator <Xwormmm> and filename-comparison value USB.exe. The host was not contacted.

Connect method RVA 0x2878 constructs a TCP socket, connects to the decrypted host/port and dispatches a host report from RVA 0x29c8. This report identifies XWorm V3.0, user/OS information and antivirus inventory. WMI inventory RVA 0x2c44 queries SecurityCenter2 AntivirusProduct and appends displayName values.

The receive callback dispatches task handler MethodDef 0x63 at RVA 0x31c8 decrypts received input, converts it to text and splits it. Plugin/savePlugin tasks recover cached or supplied assembly bytes and call MethodDef 0x64, RVA 0x3858, which invokes AppDomain.Load, locates Plugin and dispatches Run/RunRecovery/injRun methods.

StartDDos task passes a received host:port:duration string to the worker at RVA 0x3dcc. It starts twenty threads per burst. Closure lambda opens a TCP socket, sends POST headers advertising Content-length 5235 without that body, sleeps 2500 ms and disposes the socket. This is intentional resource-exhaustion tasking, not ordinary HTTP.

The $Cap branch of MethodDef 0x63 calls CopyFromScreen, resizes to 256x156, saves a JPEG to stream local 13, obtains that same local via ToArray, compresses it with helper 0xb6, converts it to text and sends #CAP through MethodDef 0x3b at RVA 0x2f50. The sender encrypts and length-prefixes data before Socket.BeginSend. No Base64 encoder is used by this variant, explaining the prior screen-theft coverage miss.

PCShutdown, PCRestart and PCLogoff dispatch shutdown.exe commands through Microsoft.VisualBasic.Interaction.Shell. MethodDef 0x94 at RVA 0x42e0 writes a delayed batch that changes to the executable directory, deletes the current executable name, changes to temp and deletes itself. It launches that batch with CreateNoWindow and Hidden settings after removing the Run key; update mode additionally starts the replacement payload.

The family command vocabulary corroborates identity. Covert command processing, exhaustion attacks and screen theft tip the malicious verdict; no deployment authorization or runtime success is established.

samples.marker_line: CI workflow: secret exposure without theft; retain suspicious risk
evidence: The entire 360-byte file is a workflow on pull_request_target opened events. It checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha and subsequently invokes ./.github/actions/integration-test with secrets.INTEGRATION_TOKEN. There is no approval gate.

The local action source and deployment provenance are absent. The file contains neither a collection/exfiltration sink nor a malicious command or alteration of a legitimate workflow. A vulnerable integration test is a sufficient benign explanation. On balance this is BENIGN with a real suspicious secret-exposure risk, not demonstrated credential theft.

The former hostile finding, including its OIDC/write-permission variants, merely combines configuration properties. Its complete matcher is retained under metadata/build/ci/gate at suspicious. The proximity atom is renamed without matcher/severity/scope changes because it does not prove a composite-action type or a same-input data flow.

samples.identification: AES-wrapped PowerShell crypter and native-host hollowing launcher
samples.marker_line: PowerShell crypter: hollows Framework host; add polling coverage
evidence: The outer script Base64-decodes ciphertext/key/IV, decrypts AES-256 CBC with PKCS7, converts bytes to UTF-8 and creates and immediately invokes a ScriptBlock over the recovered text. Recovered source length is 1131030 bytes.

The decoded script probes aspnet_compiler process liveness. When absent, it Base64-decodes a blob, XORs bytes with a repeating UTF-8 mask, Base64-decodes the resulting text into a 64000-byte managed assembly, and calls reflected FILE.WHORE.LAUNCHER with Framework v4 aspnet_compiler.exe and a 286208-byte native PE. It polls again after a variable five-second default sleep.

Token-resolved CIL establishes that LAUNCHER RVA 0x207c retries qASnOg2Lc. The static constructor at RVA 0x27a0 constructs an ordered twelve-delegate pipeline. The pipeline creates a native host with flags 0x08000004, parses the supplied PE headers, initializes a 179-int i386 context with flags 0x10002, reads the PEB image-base pointer at context Ebx+8, optionally unmaps, allocates remote memory with 0x3000 and protection 0x40, copies headers and section data, updates the PEB image-base slot, sets context Eax (array index 44) to mapped base plus entry RVA, restores context and resumes the thread.

Protected string/API resolution is corroborated by LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress ImplMap entries and typed delegate argument layouts. The native image has an MZ-header entry trampoline and entry RVA 0x26e0, whose path enters an obfuscated routine at RVA 0x1090. That routine scans stack data and XOR-transforms bytes via a stored pointer. Its final unpacked application identity is unresolved; no stealing or persistence after reboot is attributed to that image.

Layered concealment, execution transplantation into a trusted Framework host, and process-liveness-based reinstallation without an ordinary product context tip the malicious verdict. Existing hostile traits cover decrypted script activation, reflective managed activation and host-image transplantation. A new neutral trait records process-query/loop/delay co-occurrence without asserting reboot persistence or network beaconing.
